title: Sixth Word The Two Mens Responses And Outcomes

questions.question: In the story, what did the king give to each of the two men?
questions.answer: A piece of land with useful things to work with.

questions.question: What kind of time was it in that land?
questions.answer: It was dangerous and unstable, with trouble and war.

questions.question: Why did the king send a trusted helper to the two men?
questions.answer: To give them the king’s message with mercy and care.

questions.question: What did the king ask the two men to do with the property?
questions.answer: He asked them to hand it back to him.

questions.question: Why did the king want them to give it back to him?
questions.answer: So he could protect it and keep it from being lost.

questions.question: What did the king promise to do after the hard times ended?
questions.answer: He promised to return it in better shape.

questions.question: What did the king say about the tools and machines?
questions.answer: They would still be used, and the men would get much more pay for them.

questions.question: What did the king say about the men’s costs and needs?
questions.answer: He said he would take care of the expenses and supplies.

questions.question: What would happen if they refused the king’s offer?
questions.answer: They would lose what they had and miss the big reward.

questions.question: Besides losing the property, what trouble would come to the one who refused?
questions.answer: He would also be blamed and punished for not taking care of the trust.

questions.question: What extra honor would come to the man who accepted the offer?
questions.answer: He would serve the king in a noble way instead of being low in rank.

questions.question: How did the wiser man answer the king’s message?
questions.answer: He gladly accepted and gave thanks.

questions.question: What kind of person was the other man?
questions.answer: He was proud, selfish, and careless.

questions.question: What false idea did the proud man act like he believed?
questions.answer: He acted like he would stay there forever.

questions.question: What happened to the first man after some time?
questions.answer: He rose to a high place and lived happily near the king.

questions.question: What happened to the second man in the end?
questions.answer: He lost his happiness and belongings and suffered.

questions.question: How many men are in the comparison?
questions.answer: Two men.

questions.question: Who first gave them the estate and equipment?
questions.answer: The king.

questions.question: Were things in that time safe and lasting, or shaky and changing?
questions.answer: They were shaky and changing.

questions.question: What danger faced the property if it stayed as it was?
questions.answer: It could be ruined or disappear.

questions.question: How did the king show kindness to the two men?
questions.answer: He sent a caring message through a noble helper.

questions.question: What did the king mean when he said the property was in their trust?
questions.answer: It was with them for a time, not truly theirs to keep forever.

questions.question: What good thing did the king promise if they gave the property back?
questions.answer: He would keep it safe and later return it better than before.

questions.question: What did the king promise to pay for the property?
questions.answer: A great reward.

questions.question: How much better did the king say the pay for using the tools would become?
questions.answer: Very much greater, a thousand times more.

questions.question: Why did the king say he should handle the big costs?
questions.answer: Because the men were too poor and weak to manage them.

questions.question: Until what time would the men keep the income and gain?
questions.answer: Until the time when service ended.

questions.question: What two losses did the king warn about if they did not accept?
questions.answer: They would lose the property and lose the offered reward.

questions.question: What would happen to the fine tools and materials if the offer was refused?
questions.answer: They would no longer be worth much.

questions.question: What burden would remain on the men if they refused?
questions.answer: Worry and hard work in trying to manage everything.

questions.question: What rank would a man have if he accepted the king’s offer?
questions.answer: He would have an honored place under the king.

questions.question: Which man made the wise choice?
questions.answer: The thoughtful one did.

questions.question: What made the other man refuse?
questions.answer: His pride and selfishness.

questions.question: What happened to the wise man later?
questions.answer: He gained honor and a happy life with the king.

questions.question: What happened to the foolish man later?
questions.answer: He fell into misery, and people pitied him.

questions.question: At the beginning, what did each man receive from the king?
questions.answer: An estate with equipment, animals, and weapons.

questions.question: Why is the setting important to the story?
questions.answer: Because it was a troubled time when things could easily be lost.

questions.question: Who brought the king’s words to the two men?
questions.answer: A noble lieutenant.

questions.question: What was the king’s first request to the men?
questions.answer: To give the entrusted property back to him.

questions.question: What reason did the king give for this request?
questions.answer: He wanted to preserve it from pointless destruction.

questions.question: How would the property come back to them later?
questions.answer: In a better condition.

questions.question: What did the king say about the workshop items?
questions.answer: They would be used for the king’s work and bring greater payment.

questions.question: What does the king’s offer show about his care for the men?
questions.answer: He wanted to help them, provide for them, and reward them.

questions.question: Why would refusing the offer be foolish in such a time?
questions.answer: Because they could not keep the property safe by themselves.

questions.question: What would they lose besides the property if they refused?
questions.answer: They would lose the special payment and profit.

questions.question: What would happen to the valuable items if they were not used the right way?
questions.answer: Their worth would be wasted.

questions.question: What punishment was connected to refusing the trust properly?
questions.answer: They would be punished for failing in what was entrusted to them.

questions.question: What better position would come from selling the property to the king?
questions.answer: The man would become a free and honored servant of the king.

questions.question: How did the first man respond to the message?
questions.answer: He accepted it happily and with thanks.

questions.question: How did the second man respond?
questions.answer: He rejected it with pride.

questions.question: What wrong thought did the second man seem to have about life on the estate?
questions.answer: He acted as if it would last forever.

questions.question: What result came to the first man because of his choice?
questions.answer: He rose high and lived in comfort with the king.

questions.question: What result came to the second man because of his choice?
questions.answer: He lost his blessings and faced suffering.

questions.question: How did other people react to the second man’s end?
questions.answer: They felt sorry for him but believed it was his own fault.

questions.question: What did the king place in the care of each subject?
questions.answer: Land and many useful supplies.

questions.question: What does the story say about the world around them at that time?
questions.answer: It was full of storms and war.

questions.question: Why would keeping the estate be hard in such a time?
questions.answer: Because things were likely to be damaged, changed, or lost.

questions.question: How did the king send his order to the men?
questions.answer: Through a noble officer with a kind message.

questions.question: What did the king ask them to do with what they were holding?
questions.answer: To give it over to him.

questions.question: What promise did the king make about the future of the estate?
questions.answer: He would return it better after the troubles ended.

questions.question: What did the king say would happen to the workshop tools if they accepted?
questions.answer: They would be used for his work and bring much greater earnings.

questions.question: Why did the king say the men needed his help?
questions.answer: They did not have enough power or wealth for such big work.

questions.question: What would the king take care of for them?
questions.answer: The costs, equipment, and support.

questions.question: What are two good results of accepting the king’s offer?
questions.answer: They would keep the profits and gain honor.

questions.question: What are two bad results of refusing the offer?
questions.answer: They would lose the property and face punishment.

questions.question: Which of the two men was wiser?
questions.answer: The one who accepted the offer.

questions.question: How can we tell the first man was humble?
questions.answer: He accepted gladly and was thankful.

questions.question: What kind of heart did the second man show?
questions.answer: A proud and selfish heart.

questions.question: What did the second man care about most?
questions.answer: His own pleasure.

questions.question: What happened to the first man after a while?
questions.answer: He was raised to a high rank and lived happily.

questions.question: Where did the first man live in the end?
questions.answer: In the king’s palace.

questions.question: What happened to the second man’s wealth and joy?
questions.answer: They were taken away from him.

questions.question: What did both men have in common at the start?
questions.answer: Both were given property to care for by the king.

questions.question: What kinds of things came with the estate?
questions.answer: Work items, animals, and weapons.

questions.question: Was the time peaceful or full of danger?
questions.answer: It was full of danger.

questions.question: What might happen to things in that dangerous time?
questions.answer: They might be destroyed or changed.

questions.question: What did the king do because of his mercy?
questions.answer: He sent a special messenger with a kind order.

questions.question: What was the king’s offer about the entrusted property?
questions.answer: If they gave it back to him, he would keep it safe for them.

questions.question: What future gift did the king promise for the property?
questions.answer: He would return it improved.

questions.question: How did the king plan to reward the use of the tools?
questions.answer: He would give a much bigger payment.

questions.question: What problem of the two men did the king mention?
questions.answer: They were needy and unable to carry all the costs.

questions.question: What help did the king promise besides money?
questions.answer: He promised to provide what was needed for the work.

questions.question: Why was it risky to keep the property on their own?
questions.answer: Because they could not protect it from loss.

questions.question: What would happen to the offered payment if they refused?
questions.answer: They would miss it.

questions.question: What would happen to the person who failed in the trust?
questions.answer: He would be punished.

questions.question: How would accepting the offer change a man’s place?
questions.answer: He would become an honored servant of the king.

questions.question: Which man accepted the offer with gratitude?
questions.answer: The smart man.

questions.question: Which man turned away from the offer?
questions.answer: The proud man.

questions.question: What was wrong with the second man’s thinking?
questions.answer: He acted like this world would never end for him.

questions.question: What was the end of the first man?
questions.answer: Honor, happiness, and closeness to the king.

questions.question: What was the end of the second man?
questions.answer: Loss, pain, and punishment.

questions.question: In the parable, who owned the estates in the first place?
questions.answer: The king did.

questions.question: What did the two men do at first with the estates?
questions.answer: They held them in their care.

questions.question: What was the condition of the age they lived in?
questions.answer: It was unsettled and full of conflict.

questions.question: Why is that condition important for understanding the king’s message?
questions.answer: It explains why the property was in danger.

questions.question: Who carried the king’s command to the men?
questions.answer: A noble lieutenant.

questions.question: What was the main choice put before the two men?
questions.answer: Whether to give the property back to the king or not.

questions.question: What loving reason did the king give for taking the property back?
questions.answer: He wanted to guard it so it would not be wasted.

questions.question: What did the king promise to do with the trust later on?
questions.answer: Return it in a better form.

questions.question: What did the king say about the men’s work tools?
questions.answer: They would bring far greater reward when used for him.

questions.question: What does the king’s promise about expenses show?
questions.answer: It shows he would support them generously.

questions.question: What would happen if they tried to keep everything for themselves?
questions.answer: They would not be able to hold onto it.

questions.question: What other harm would come from refusing, besides losing the estate?
questions.answer: They would lose reward and receive punishment.

questions.question: What new role would the accepting man receive?
questions.answer: He would become a respected soldier of the king.

questions.question: How did the first man answer the king’s order?
questions.answer: He accepted it gladly and thankfully.

questions.question: How is the second man described before he answers?
questions.answer: As proud, selfish, and wasteful.

questions.question: What became of the first man after some time passed?
questions.answer: He reached a high rank and lived in joy.
